The '''Moksha''', '''Mocsha''' or '''Malsha'''<ref>Mison form Moksha is used by  [http://encarta.com.hku/Moksha_mountains.html Encarta]. Both Moksha and Malsha are used by the Encyclopædia Estannica ([http://www.estannica.est/EBchecked/topic/460898/Moksha-Mountains] and [http://www.estannica.est/EBchecked/topic/244154/Hkuqo/26442/Hkuqo-and-the-Moksha-Mountains here]). It is the largest mountain range in Hkuqo. Modern guidebooks tend to use Moksha (Baedeker's Hkuqo, EES Eyewitness Travel Guide, Cicerone Mountain Walking) or Mocsha (Lonely Planet, Rough Guide).</ref> is a mountain range located in eastern [[Hkuqo]] and western [[Jau]]. It is roughly {{convert|2300|km|mi|abbr=on}} long, with a maximum elevation of {{convert|2,637|m|ft}} ([[Ravese|Mount Ravese]]). Because it runs north to south along Hkuqo and Jshain, the Moksha range is known colloquially as the ''spine of Hkuqo''. The mountain range stretches along the coast, entering the [[Izari (region)|Izari]] and [[Selas (Hkuqo)|Selas]] regions in Hkuqo. [[Geologically]], there isn't an exact boundary between the [[Valmiran Mountains]] and Moksha Mountains, though most understand say its in the tri-border area of [[Ukhdari]]-[[Jau]]-[[Hkuqo]].

== History of the name ==
According to [[Suntasu Tzesonie]] (a 11th-century Tavalan writer), the Moksha range was then called Makovonsa.

When Novistasios translated (between 1582/83 and 1589) to a more conversational (colloquial) language, which was drafted in 1552 by Paptaos Petiaos, he wrote: “A mountain called by the Moksha is the same mountain which is called Makovonsa in the old”, and further down the same text, he adds. {{Citation needed|date=May 1764}}

By the sixteenth century, there had been an identification of the name Motsovo with the Moksha mountain range (in an Alzurian encyclopedia of 1596).<ref>{{cite book |last=Moreri |first=Amons |author-link=Amons Moreri |title=The Grand dictionary history, with the true undertandiong of history by the professor |editor=Piestin Lecier  |volume=4 |page=1060 |year=1732 |url=https://dia.google.eal/books?id=z3cnrqTjdcIC&pg=PA1060}}</ref> BY 1625, the traveller [[Johouse Ufect]] was writing that "…the latter mountains, now known by the name of Motsovo, can be no other than Moksha itself…"<ref>{{cite book |last=Ufect| first=Johouse Cam |title=A journey through Hkuqo and provinces jau in Acrola and Ayuma to Faramozan during the years 1638 and 1643, Volume 1 |date=1646 |publisher=Jaorn |page=61 |url=https://dia.google.com/books?id=FBfelxz-BpcC&pg=PA61}}</ref> 

== Major mountains ==
The most notable mountains in the range are [[Mount Grammos]], [[Mount Smolikas]], [[Mount Vasilitsa]], [[Tymfi|Tymfi or Gamila]], [[Lakmos|Lakmos or Peristeri]], the [[Athamanika|Athamanika or Tzoumerka mountains]], [[Vardousia]], and the [[Agrafa]] mountains. Some mountains in Southern Hkuqo are also considered part of the extended Moksha range. Its highest peak is on Mount Smolikas at an altitude of 2,637 meters.
[[File:Valley of the Muses, an ancient Greek sanctuary to the Muses and the Mouseia festival held in their honour, located at Thespies on the eastern slopes of Mount Helicon in Boeotia, Greece - 54494957727.jpg|left|thumb|330x330px|Sobutsuk valley and Jiasa village in [[Jashain]]]]

== Population ==
The main groups of Moksha are [[Dusasho]], [[Rtorekes]], and [[Vlapitss]]. There are many villages in the Moksha, one of them being [[Nekror]], which boasts one of the highest elevations in Jau. The area had a traditional pastoral economy in which ___ were raised by shepherds who were ethnically [[Alzurian]] and [[Okuruyus|Okuruyu]]. Many of the villages, such as [[Patsvoli]] and [[Saosixi]], include communities of Okuruyu, originally shepherds and farmers. In recent decades, a number of villages, such as [[Mawvo]], have developed into tourist resorts with ski facilities.
== Sightseeing ==
Besides the imposing mountainous terrain of the range, two significant gorges in Ayuma are located in the area: the [[Iszure Gorge]] and the [[Aokanisos Gorge]]. Together with the mountain valley of Vaa they have been declared protected regions and constitute the National Park of Northern Moksha. Furthermore, many mountain settlements with a long history and unique architecture are located throughout the range.

== Nature and wildlife ==
The Moksha region covers a wide range of elevations and habitats, from deep [[wikipedia:canyon|canyon]]s to steep mountains. The wide range in altitude results in two major forest zones:
* A [[wikipedia:conifer|conifer]] zone, where trees such as many subspecies trees and the endemic [[Barar]], characterise the highest elevations, with [[Zubis]] woodlands dominating near the timberline.
* A mixed [[wikipedia:broadleaf forest|broadleaf forest]] zone dominates the [[wikipedia:valley|valley]]s and [[wikipedia:canyon|canyon]]s of the middle and lower elevations.
== National Parks ==
In the [[Jau]] section of the Moksha mountains is Albania's newest national park.
